subject: Re: DPA retention exceptions, temporary hold and proof-of-deletion playbook
messages:
From: Emma Moore <emma@acmecorp.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: DPA: questions on retention carveouts and temporary hold

Rachel —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Legal has a couple of follow-ups on the retention / deletion language in the DPA, specifically around:

1) Temporary lawful-hold: We need confirmation of the operational flow when Acme issues a preservation notice. Does Redwood support an immediate "freeze" on deletion timelines and a documented audit trail?

2) Backup windows: Acme wants a carveout for backups older than 90 days which may still exist for up to 180 days for restore purposes, but only if we can get certified proof of purge once the restore window closes.

3) Evidence of deletion: What can Redwood provide as a post-erasure certificate? Our compliance team prefers a small set of artifacts (tombstone manifest, deletion job IDs, signed timestamp).

Attaching a redline of the DPA with our suggested language (Acme_DPA_redline_v1.docx). Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the temporary-hold flow and what operational artifacts you can provide?

Best,
Emma
Emma Moore
Dir. Information Security, Acme Corp

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Emma Moore <emma@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA: questions on retention carveouts and temporary hold

Emma —

Thanks for the clear redline and questions. We can accept the concept of a temporary preservation notice with the following operational constraints and artifacts:

- Preservation flow: Upon receipt of a written preservation notice to legal@redwood.com and the assigned AM, we will mark the affected tenant records with a preservation flag which prevents scheduled erasure jobs from removing records. This flag propagates to snapshot/backup scheduling but does not stop ongoing write operations.

- Audit trail: We can provide an immutable event log (audit entries) for the preservation action, including timestamp, requestor identity, and the retention flag ID.

- Backup carveout: We agree to an extended backup retention window of up to 180 days for the specific classes you noted, provided the list of classes is enumerated in Appendix B. Restores will be performed on request; once the restore window is closed, we will queue the corresponding backup segment for deletion and provide a deletion manifest.

- Deletion evidence: We can produce a signed deletion manifest (job ID, object IDs truncated for PII protection, timestamp, operator) and a tombstone manifest. We cannot, however, provide raw object-level hashes for production backups due to encryption and multi-tenant storage layout constraints.

I've started a suggested redline of your doc (attached: Acme_DPA_redline_v2.docx) that keeps your preservation language but narrows the scope of artifacts to what we can operationally provide.

Next steps: Ben — can you confirm any commercial impact (credits/fees) for supporting the extended backup carveout and the operational SLA for evidence delivery? David — can you note expected engineering lead time for the preservation flag + signed-manifest workflow?

Cheers,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Head of Product (Enterprise), Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Moore <emma@acmecorp.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA: questions on retention carveouts and temporary hold

Emma / team —

Short answer on commercial impact: there is a modest operational cost here. Two items to flag:

1) Preservation monitoring + manifesting: We estimate ~0.5 FTE equivalent per large customer during the active preservation window for ops tasks and manifest generation; we usually handle this under an Enterprise add-on (one-time onboarding + monthly operational fee).

2) Longer backup retention: additional storage and snapshot management cost. For Acme's projected footprint (per our sizing exercise), ballpark is $2k–$4k/month incremental. We can convert this into a credit or committed usage tier if Acme prefers.

If you want, I can draft a short SOW addendum for the financials and the escalation matrix for preservation notices.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Acme Legal <legal@acmecorp.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Moore <emma@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Dec 2026 08:50:00 -0800
Subject: RE: DPA: questions on retention carveouts and temporary hold

Rachel / Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few follow-ups from Legal on the redline you sent:

- We need the deletion manifest to include a signed statement from an authorized Redwood officer (name + title) confirming completion. Is Redwood comfortable with a template statement (one paragraph)?
- For the preservation flag, can Redwood guarantee that the flag will be honored across all copies (primary, secondary, cold snapshots)? If not, please state which layers are covered.
- Timeline: we need the evidence (signed manifest + tombstone) within 10 business days of the deletion action. Please confirm.

Also attached is an annotated version of your redline (Acme_DPA_redline_v2.docx) — we've highlighted the officer statement and timeline.

John Patel from VendorCo is copied — we may surface a separate request about vendor-handled backups.

Regards,
Acme Legal

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Acme Legal <legal@acmecorp.com>, Emma Moore <emma@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, John Patel <john.patel@vendorco.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 17:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA: questions on retention carveouts and temporary hold — operational playbook and next steps

Legal / Emma / John —

Summary & action items after internal sync:

1) Officer-signed manifest: Redwood can provide a standard deletion certificate with a short attestation signed by our Head of Security Operations or General Counsel. The attestation will be a one-paragraph statement confirming deletion job IDs and the scope. We will include the signed name and title as requested.

2) Preservation flag coverage: The preservation flag will be applied to the logical tenant data set and will prevent scheduled erasure jobs for the primary store and warm snapshots. Cold/archival snapshots (cold-tier immutable backups handled by VendorCo) are out of scope unless VendorCo agrees in writing. John — can you confirm whether VendorCo can accept the preservation flag propagation or whether Acme needs a separate vendor-ops flow?

3) Evidence timeline: Redwood commits to delivering the signed deletion manifest and tombstone manifest within 10 business days of the deletion job completing. If there is any blocking issue (e.g., cross-vendor coordinate), we will escalate per the SOW addendum.

4) Commercials: Ben will draft an addendum outlining the operational fee and an optional committed storage credit. Ben — target to share the SOW draft by Tue 2026-12-21.

5) Engineering next steps: David will provision a preservation-flag feature branch and a manifest-generator task. Target: internal RFC / dev estimate by 2027-01-07.

Attachments: retention-evidence-matrix.xlsx (contains the classes of data we agree to extend to 180-day backup carveout and the list of artifacts we can provide).

If that all sounds acceptable, Emma — please confirm and we will circulate the SOW addendum and the updated DPA redline for final sign-off.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Head of Product (Enterprise), Redwood Inference
